root_cause.text: The hid_post_reset() function allocates memory with GFP_KERNEL, which may trigger block I/O while the device reset holds a mutex, causing a deadlock when the USB device also contains a storage component that needs I/O to complete.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explains that hid_pre_reset() and hid_post_reset() run in block IO error handling context, so allocations must not perform block IO to avoid deadlock on the held mutex; the patch changes `GFP_KERNEL` to `GFP_NOIO` in the `kmalloc` call in hid_post_reset().

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential deadlock in USB HID post-reset handler by using GFP_NOIO instead of GFP_KERNEL for memory allocation.
intent_record.what: Changed the GFP flags in kmalloc from GFP_KERNEL to GFP_NOIO when allocating memory for the HID report descriptor in hid_post_reset.
intent_record.how: This prevents the memory allocation from initiating any I/O operations, which could lead to a deadlock or recursion during USB device reset processing.

grouping_result.intent: Fix potential deadlock in USB HID post-reset handler by using GFP_NOIO instead of GFP_KERNEL for memory allocation.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly fixes the deadlock vulnerability described in the root cause by changing GFP_KERNEL to GFP_NOIO in the hid_post_reset() function to prevent I/O during reset.

candidates.rationale: Allocation with GFP_KERNEL in hid_post_reset() may trigger block I/O while holding a mutex, causing a deadlock when the USB device contains a storage component.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement allocates memory with GFP_KERNEL in the hid_post_reset() function, which may trigger block I/O while holding a mutex. If the USB device contains a storage component, this can cause a deadlock because the I/O cannot complete. The fix is to use GFP_NOIO instead.
